content.text:
Section 24 satisfies every element of our preferred position, and the planner's two concerns check out:

- **24.1** gives us consent-free assignment to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets — notice only, no consent gate.
- **24.2** binds the Vendor asymmetrically (consent required, reasonableness standard, absolute bar on assigning to a direct Customer competitor), and expressly captures delegation of material performance and Vendor transfer by change of control.
- **24.3** does not swallow 24.1: it is prefaced "For other assignments," so it operates only as a residual catch-all for transfers outside the 24.1/24.2 carve-outs, and its consent standard is reciprocal and qualified ("not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed").
- **24.4** eliminates any Vendor termination, suspension, repricing, Fee-acceleration, or service-reduction right triggered by our change of control — the walk-away risk is affirmatively closed out.
- **13.3** tracks Section 24 correctly, letting us move licence rights to an Affiliate or successor on a permitted assignment, so the licence grant will not strand a successor.

I also confirmed there is no "deemed an assignment" trap elsewhere and that the only other assignment reference (9.2) concerns insolvency-type general assignments for creditors, not our M&A activity.

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.
